title: Free libuv handles in the close callback
summary: Free clients in the close callback instead of right after uv_close, then shut down on Ctrl-C all the way to uv_loop_close.

turns.user: server sometimes dies when a client disconnects. asan says heap-use-after-free inside uv_run

assistant.body: Good instinct to look at where it dies. uv_close does not close the handle on the spot. It queues the close on the loop, finishes it on a later iteration, and only then calls the close callback. Freeing before that leaves libuv touching freed memory. The idiomatic pattern is to free in the close callback, placed above on_read.

turns.user: fixed. now i want ctrl-c to exit cleanly, call uv_loop_close too

assistant.body: Catching SIGINT with a uv_signal_t, stopping the loop with uv_stop, then calling uv_loop_close. This guarantees a clean, deterministic shutdown.

turns.user: it prints loop close: resource busy or locked

assistant.body: Apologies, that shutdown was wrong. uv_stop only leaves the loop and every handle stays open, so uv_loop_close returns UV_EBUSY. Instead of stopping, close every handle and let uv_run return on its own. The server and the signal live on the stack, so they close with NULL. The remaining clients are found with uv_walk and freed by on_close. The server is reached through sig.data.
